title: Coherent monads and the weighted module infinity-category
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, nerves and coherent functor simplicial sets from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in an ambient universe large enough for all the following simplicial sets. Let $\Delta_+$ be the category of finite ordered sets, including the empty set, and weakly increasing maps, with ordinal sum $\oplus$ and empty unit. Put $D=N(\Delta_+)$. A coherent monad on a quasicategory $\mathcal C$ is a simplicial action $t:D\times\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ which preserves ordinal sum and its empty unit: $t(u\oplus v,c)=t(u,t(v,c))$ and $t(\varnothing,c)=c$ in every simplicial degree. Equivalently this is a simplicial functor from the walking monad, the homotopy coherent model of a unital associative algebra in the endofunctor infinity-category under composition. Its endofunctor $T$ is evaluation at the singleton ordinal; $\eta$ is evaluation on the unique empty-to-singleton map and $\mu$ on the two-element-to-singleton map. Let $\Delta_\infty$ be the category of nonempty finite ordered sets with monotone maps preserving the last element and put $W=N(\Delta_\infty)$, included in $D$ by $i$. Ordinal sum gives a left $D$-action on $W$. Explicitly, its graph is $P=(D\times W)\times_D W$, where the first map is $(d,w)\mapsto d\oplus i(w)$ and the second is $i$. The coherent module simplicial set $\operatorname{Alg}_T(\mathcal C)$ is the equalizer of the two maps $\operatorname{Fun}(W,\mathcal C)\rightrightarrows\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal C)$ given by $b\mapsto((d,w,w')\mapsto b(w'))$ and $b\mapsto((d,w,w')\mapsto t(d,b(w)))$. This is the actual equivariant internal hom, retaining coherent module maps and their higher simplices. Its forgetful map $V$ evaluates at the singleton in $W$. The free underlying algebra diagram is $c\mapsto(w\mapsto t(i(w),c))$, and the powers $T^n$ are iterates of $T$, with $T^0=1$.

source.place: Riehl--Verity, Homotopy coherent adjunctions and the formal theory of monads, Adv. Math. 286 (2016), §§3.3.6, 6.1.1--6.1.10 and 6.1.14; the explicit model for HA §§4.2.3--4.2.4, applied to End(C).
